note: Every curve the plausibility screen flags must be listed here with a reason, or scripts/screen_outliers.py fails. Listing is triage, not a verdict that the curve is right: 'Not explained' entries are open leads.

triaged.dubois21.newhorizon.bh-mbh.z1: Per-black-hole points within 2 R_eff against population medians in the peers; not like for like.
triaged.diemer19.tng300.h2-fraction.z0: Median over galaxies above the detection threshold only; band is the spread across nine HI-H2 models. Not explained: check against the paper.
triaged.schaye23.flamingo-l1_m10.gsmf.z0: Includes 0.3 dex mock scatter and covers only the steep high-mass segment; expected.
triaged.baker25.qsmf.z2.5-3: Quiescent-only mass function, flagged as not comparable with total mass functions in the record; expected.
triaged.katz23.sphinx20.size.uv-1500A.z5: UV-1500A size against half-mass radii in the peers: a different size definition; expected.
triaged.katz23.sphinx20.size.uv-1500A.z6: UV-1500A size against half-mass radii in the peers: a different size definition; expected.
triaged.katz23.sphinx20.size.uv-1500A.z7: UV-1500A size against half-mass radii in the peers: a different size definition; expected.
triaged.magneticum.box2hr.jstar.z0.official: Morphology and aperture not specified in the table header. Not explained: a real lead for the Magneticum authors.
triaged.schaye23.flamingo-l1_m10.size-active-ap1: Projected half-mass radius in a 100 kpc 2D aperture, active galaxies; probably a definition difference.
triaged.camels.simba.ssfr-dist.cv.z0: Median over all subhaloes, quiescent ones included (the distribution record's median, not a star-forming main sequence); in SIMBA the median falls to log sSFR -11.6 at 10^10.4 Msun because most galaxies there are quenched, so it sits far below the star-forming medians of the peers. Expected for this definition; the distribution view shows the shares.
triaged.vcd.bauer-et-al-2013-gama.all-galaxies.s: The median sSFR of all GAMA galaxies (Bauer+13) lies about 1.2 dex below the median of all galaxies in GSWLC-2 (Salim+18) at the same mass and redshift (log sSFR -11.3 against -10.1 at 10^10 Msun). Both are labelled population 'all'; the SFR indicators differ (H-alpha against SED fitting with UV and infrared) and the Bauer statistic and treatment of galaxies without a detection are not stated in the compilation. Not explained: check against the paper before reading this as a tension between observations.
triaged.dubois21.newhorizon.bh-secondary.z0.25: Per-black-hole points of secondary black holes within 2 R_eff against population medians in the peers; not like for like (the same reading as dubois21.newhorizon.bh-mbh.z1).
triaged.dubois21.newhorizon.bh-mbh.z2: Per-black-hole points within 2 R_eff against population medians in the peers; not like for like (the same reading as dubois21.newhorizon.bh-mbh.z1).
triaged.darwin1.catalogue.bh.z4: Median black hole mass of galaxies that hold at least one black hole particle (summed over particles; galaxies without one are left out) in 4 bins, against peers that are medians over central galaxies; the selection raises the median, so not like for like. Not explained: how much of the 2 dex is the selection and how much the seed mass; the paper shows this relation at z = 2.1 and 0.19 only.
triaged.katz23.sphinx20.shmr.virial.z8: Checked against the data release and the paper on 2026-10-25 (internal check, no outside review; scripts/check_sphinx20_release.py). The halo-mass definition and unit are right. The release column mvir is log10 of the virial mass in Msun, not Msun/h: the paper's printed Table 1 is reproduced (7 galaxy counts and 28 log masses, within the printed rounding); the paper's stellar-mass against halo-mass figure (both axes in Msun) is reproduced by the release columns as they are (1380 of 1380 galaxies within 0.0001 dex of a plotted marker); the paper's halo mass function figure, which is in Msun/h and per (cMpc/h)^3, is reproduced count for count (50 of 50 plotted bins) only with mvir times h and a box of 20 cMpc. The virial mass and radius of the release imply one overdensity, 205 times the critical density at z = 4.64 to 6 and 179 at z = 7 to 10 (Bryan and Norman: about 177), a spherical virial mass; the stellar mass is the total mass formed, not reduced for stellar mass loss (the paper's table note). So the offset is in the sample and the model, not in a unit. (1) Only haloes that host a galaxy with SFR(10 Myr) >= 0.3 Msun/yr are in the release. Read from the paper's halo mass function figure at z = 8, the release holds 0.0 to 6.9 % of the haloes below log Mvir = 9.46 (Msun), 15 to 41 % between 9.46 and 9.88, 72 to 77 % between 9.88 and 10.30 and all of them above (5 haloes); the lower bins of this record are medians of the star-forming minority (the paper: 'biased (by construction) towards star-forming galaxies'). (2) In the two highest bins (log Mvir 9.875 and 10.125, 23 and 17 galaxies, where the release holds 41 to 77 % of the haloes) the record is still 1.2 to 1.6 dex above ASTRID, CoDa II and THESAN-1. That remainder is not explained: the peers' haloes are Friends-of-Friends (ASTRID, CoDa II) or unspecified (THESAN-1) and their medians run over all haloes, a difference of definition not measured here, and the release is one 20 cMpc box with one set of subgrid choices.
triaged.katz23.sphinx20.shmr.virial.z6: Checked against the data release and the paper on 2026-10-25 (internal check, no outside review; scripts/check_sphinx20_release.py). The halo-mass definition and unit are right. The release column mvir is log10 of the virial mass in Msun, not Msun/h: the paper's printed Table 1 is reproduced (7 galaxy counts and 28 log masses, within the printed rounding); the paper's stellar-mass against halo-mass figure (both axes in Msun) is reproduced by the release columns as they are (1380 of 1380 galaxies within 0.0001 dex of a plotted marker); the paper's halo mass function figure, which is in Msun/h and per (cMpc/h)^3, is reproduced count for count (50 of 50 plotted bins) only with mvir times h and a box of 20 cMpc. The virial mass and radius of the release imply one overdensity, 205 times the critical density at z = 4.64 to 6 and 179 at z = 7 to 10 (Bryan and Norman: about 177), a spherical virial mass; the stellar mass is the total mass formed, not reduced for stellar mass loss (the paper's table note). So the offset is in the sample and the model, not in a unit. (1) Only haloes that host a galaxy with SFR(10 Myr) >= 0.3 Msun/yr are in the release. Read from the paper's halo mass function figure, the release holds 0.0 to 3.9 % of the haloes below log Mvir = 9.46 (Msun), 13 to 20 % between 9.46 and 9.88, 54 % between 9.88 and 10.09, 73 % between 10.09 and 10.30, 86 % between 10.30 and 10.51 and all of them above; the lower bins of this record are medians of the star-forming minority (the paper: 'biased (by construction) towards star-forming galaxies'). (2) In the two bins where the release holds about 80 to 100 % of the haloes (log Mvir 10.375 and 10.625; the bin of 10.375 spans the 73 % and 86 % bins of the figure) the record is still 1.1 to 1.5 dex above ASTRID, CoDa II and THESAN-1, and the paper's own figure puts the release median 0.5 dex above the Tacchella et al. 2018 model at 10^10.5 Msun. That remainder is not explained: the peers' haloes are Friends-of-Friends (ASTRID, CoDa II) or unspecified (THESAN-1) and their medians run over all haloes, a difference of definition not measured here, and the release is one 20 cMpc box with one set of subgrid choices.
triaged.ocvirk20.coda2.shmr.z10: Median over all Friends-of-Friends haloes above 1e8 Msun, including haloes that hold no stars, in 4 bins, against peers that are medians over central galaxies; the population pulls the median down, so not like for like.
triaged.schaye23.flamingo-gsmf.mstar-s-fgas-4s.z: Agrees with the other sources' median within 0.3 dex up to log M* = 11.5 (checked at 10, 11 and 11.5); the median offset of about -0.75 dex over the whole curve comes from the massive end, where the 1 cGpc box falls 1.2 to 1.4 dex below the peers at 12.0 and 2.9 to 4.1 dex below at 12.3 to 12.4, and fewer than 20 mostly small-box peers (spread 0.7 dex) reach there. Where the exponential tail should lie is not settled here; the curve is the paper's.
